narrative:
Based on the information you provided, our assessment indicates a 63% chance that you would represent a bad credit risk. This means that, in the bank's view, there is a high likelihood you would struggle to repay the loan, and that is why your application was denied.

The most important factor in this decision was your checking account status. Your account currently has a negative balance, meaning it is overdrawn. Among previously approved applicants, only about one in eight had a negative balance—most had no balance or a positive one. This was the single strongest signal pushing toward a denial.

Your loan duration also worked against you. You requested to repay the loan over 24 months, which is longer than the average of roughly 19 months among approved borrowers. Longer repayment periods increase the chance that something goes wrong, so this pushed your application further toward the bad-risk category.

On the positive side, the amount you requested—1,659 DM—is well below the average loan amount of about 3,020 DM. This actually helped your case, since smaller loans are generally less risky. However, the negative influence of your overdrawn account and the longer duration outweighed this benefit.

To improve your chances in the future, I recommend focusing on bringing your checking account into positive territory and maintaining it there for several months. Consider applying for a shorter loan term and, if possible, a smaller amount. Rebuilding a stable financial record first will make a meaningful difference.
